title: Bibimbap
subtitle: Korean mixed rice bowl with vegetables, egg, and gochujang
excerpt: Bibimbap (mixed rice) is one of the most famous Korean dishes: a bowl of steamed rice topped with seasoned vegetables, a fried or raw egg, and gochujang (Korean chilli paste). Each topping is prepared separately. The beauty of the dish is in the variety of textures and flavours brought together when the rice and toppings are mixed at the table.
sourceNotes: Bibimbap (literally 'mixed rice') has been documented in Korean records since the Joseon dynasty. The dish is considered one of the great representations of Korean culinary philosophy: the harmonious balance of the five colours (red, green, yellow, white, and black) and five flavours. Dolsot bibimbap, served in a hot stone pot, is the form most associated with restaurant presentation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The vegetable toppings can be prepared up to 2 days ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: The vegetables in bibimbap are each cooked and seasoned separately: this preserves their distinct flavours and textures. Use whatever combination you have, but aim for at least 4 different toppings in different colours. The gochujang sauce is mixed at the table; each person adjusts the heat to their taste.

items.prepNote: 3 tbsp for seasoning vegetables, 1 tbsp for the gochujang sauce

content.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain, cool under cold water, squeeze out all the moisture. Season with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon sesame oil. Set aside in a small bowl.
Stir-fry each remaining vegetable separately in a little oil for 2 to 3 minutes until just cooked. Season each with a little soy sauce and sesame oil. Keep separate.
Make the gochujang sauce and assemble
Mix together the gochujang, 2 teaspoons sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sugar with 2 tablespoons of water. Stir until smooth.

Cook the rice. Fry the eggs in a little oil: sunny-side up, yolk still runny. Divide the hot rice between 4 bowls. Arrange the vegetables in sections around the edge. Place a fried egg in the centre. Add 1 tablespoon of gochujang sauce. Scatter with sesame seeds. Mix everything together at the table.

items.symptom: Vegetables are wet and sitting in liquid at the bottom of the bowl
items.cause: Vegetables not squeezed dry after blanching, or not cooked long enough to evaporate moisture
items.fix: The spinach must be firmly squeezed dry. Other vegetables should be stir-fried on high heat to evaporate their moisture, not just warmed through.
